In Escambia the appraiser sets the value and the collector sends the invoice. The Property Appraiser maintains the roll for Escambia County, the City of Pensacola and the Town of Century, and its site labels assessed values and exemptions as the 2026 certified tax roll.

The Tax Collector gathers money for the District School Board, the Board of County Commissioners, Pensacola, Century, the Sheriff, the Downtown Improvement Board and the Northwest Florida Water Management District, plus several state agencies. You can look up a bill by name, address or account number, and the site offers paperless e-billing and tax reports.

The street address decides your total, because the Tax Collector prints a separate stack of levies for each part of the county. One mill is a tenth of a cent per dollar of taxable value.

2026 millage by area
AreaLines in the stackTotal mills
City of PensacolaCounty 6.5710, schools 5.3540, city 4.2895, water district 0.0201, library 0.3590, children's trust 0.366116.9597

Unincorporated countyCounty, schools, water district, Sheriff 0.6850, library, children's trust13.3552
Pensacola BeachCounty, schools, water district, library, children's trust12.6702

The school line has two parts: 2.2480 set by the local board and 3.1060 set by state law. Only the unincorporated column carries a Sheriff line, so a house outside city limits pays for that service through its own levy, and the Pensacola stack leaves it out.

Notices go out November 1 to whoever owned the property on January 1. Paying early earns a discount that shrinks by a point each month, from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. March is full price.

  • April 1: delinquent. Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty, tangible property 1.5 percent.
  • May 1: advertising costs start to accrue.
  • A bill that never arrived is no excuse. The owner must find out the amount, even when mail went to an old address.

If you move, send the new mailing address to the Property Appraiser, because the roll lives there.

Owners who paid more than $100 of tax the prior year and have no mortgage escrow can split the bill. Applications open online January 1 and close April 30 for that cycle.

  • First payment by June 30, with a 6 percent discount.
  • Second by September 30, with 4.5 percent off.
  • Third by December 31, with 3 percent off.
  • Fourth by March 31, with no discount.

The first two payments each equal a quarter of last year's tax. The last two divide the actual balance. Miss the June payment and the plan ends, and a regular November bill follows. Partial payments toward a current bill can be accepted at the collector's discretion, but they need an application, earn no discount and cannot be made after March 31.

The Duplicate Tax Notice Request Program lets you name a relative or friend to get a courtesy copy of every bill. Mail the signed application to the Collections Department, P.O. Box 1312, Pensacola, FL 32591-1312.

Some lines ignore your home's value, yet unpaid amounts can still lead to a certificate. Where the parcel sits decides which ones appear.

  • Unincorporated Escambia: fire protection, rescue and advanced life support, street lighting, road paving, retention ponds and solid waste, all assessed by the county commissioners.
  • Inside Pensacola: stormwater, based on the impervious surface on the lot, assessed by the City Council.

Title agents ask about these at closing, so read the bottom of the bill as well as the millage section.

A permanent residence can have up to $50,000 taken off its taxable value. File Form DR-501 with the Property Appraiser by March 1. After the first year, assessed value rises under a cap, shown at 2.7 percent on the state's 2026 chart.

A sale restarts the clock. The buyer is assessed at market value from the following January, while portability may move part of your cap to a replacement Florida home.

The process begins with the proposed-tax notice that arrives in August. A petition on Form DR-486 must reach the clerk within 25 days of the mailing. The same notice lists budget hearing dates for the school board, the county and Pensacola.

A denied exemption goes the other way, through the Value Adjustment Board, and you have 30 days from the mailing of the denial letter. Keep every notice.

Before you call or file, collect your August notice, a copy of your deed and anything that supports your number, such as a recent appraisal or photos of damage. Write down who you spoke with and when. A short, specific request tends to get a faster answer than a general complaint.

After April 1 a certificate can be sold on the parcel, and a deed application may follow later. The Tax Collector warns that nonpayment can cost you the property.

  • Investors bid the interest rate down in quarter-point steps.
  • A deed application must wait two years and carries a $75 fee.
  • For a homestead, the opening deed bid adds half the latest assessed figure.

Closing with a certificate attached is routine. The title agent pays the redemption out of the seller's side of the statement.

Seniors, disabled owners and military families each have their own forms. A service-connected disabled veteran aged 65 or more may receive a homestead discount matching the VA rating. A disabled former servicemember gets $5,000 off assessed value. Deferral requests go to the Tax Collector by March 31. Ask the appraiser which local senior options the county offers.

Ask the Tax Collector's office for every account under your name, including a Business Tax Receipt if you rented the property or ran a business there. Deed stamps are 70 cents for every hundred dollars of price, paid at the clerk. If your lender escrows, find out what it paid and how quickly any refund arrives. An inherited house may need clerk estate records before a title agent will insure it.

A plain order of events helps. Request the payoff first, then give it to the closing agent along with your ID and loan information. The agent pays the tax and any other liens from your proceeds and sends you a final statement. Compare that statement with the collector's figure before you sign, and keep a copy for your own records.

faqs.q: What do the 2026 millage lines add up to inside Pensacola?
faqs.a: The City of Pensacola area totals 16.9597 mills, built from county, school, city, water district, library and children's trust lines. Unincorporated parcels total 13.3552.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Escambia installment plan?
faqs.a: Owners who paid more than $100 in tax the year before and have no escrow. The application closes April 30, and a missed June 30 first payment ends the plan.

faqs.q: Does the Escambia homestead cap pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer starts at market value the next January. Portability can carry some of your cap to another Florida home.

faqs.q: Can a relative get copies of my Escambia bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Duplicate Tax Notice Request Program you name a relative or friend, then mail the signed form to the Collections Department, P.O. Box 1312, Pensacola, FL 32591-1312.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Escambia house that has a tax certificate on it?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing redeems the certificate from your proceeds. Get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector before the closing date.
